rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order puts crops before trees because grain is food, while tree produce is fruit and food precedes fruit.
rows.anchor: قدم الزرع على الشجر لأن الزرع غذاء ، وثمار الأشجار فواكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The date palm precedes other fruit trees because dates serve Arabs as food and philosophers note its unusual resemblance to animals in many properties.
rows.anchor: قدم النخل على سائر الفواكه لأن التمر يجري مجرى الغذاء بالنسبة إلى العرب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic saying calls the palm the paternal aunt of plants and says it was created from what remained of Adam's clay; Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( أكرموا عمتكم النخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls grape king of fruits: its shoots, sour unripe grapes and ripe fruit each have uses; hanging grapes store well and yield raisins, syrup, wine and vinegar; wine is forbidden despite acknowledged benefit (2:219), and seed preparations aid weak moist stomachs.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن العنب كأنه سلطان الفواكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Olives are useful eaten whole and also yield abundant oil for food and many other uses.
rows.anchor: يمكن تناوله كما هو ، وينفصل أيضا عنه دهن كثير عظيم النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pomegranate is a compound body with four parts: rind, pith, seeds and juice.
rows.anchor: جسم مركب من أربعة أقسام : قشره وشحمه وعجمه وماؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rind, pith and seeds are dense, cold, dry, earthy and astringent, while juice is their opposite: light, balanced, pleasant, strengthening, both food and medicine; their union displays divine power and mercy.
rows.anchor: فكلها باردة يابسة أرضية كثيفة قابضة عفصة قوية في هذه الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since plant kinds are too numerous to describe, God names four of the noblest as a cue to the rest.
rows.anchor: أنواع النبات أكثر من أن تفي بشرحها مجلدات ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that fruits may match in color and shape yet differ in taste, or differ in appearance yet share flavor and pleasure.
rows.anchor: قد تكون متشابهة في اللون والشكل ، مع أنها تكون مختلفة في الطعم واللذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that peel and seeds across many fruits resemble one another in taste and properties, while their flesh and moisture differ in taste.
rows.anchor: أن أكثر الفواكه يكون ما فيها من القشر والعجم متشابها في الطعم والخاصية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says tree leaves are similar to one another, whereas their fruits differ.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : أوراق الأشجار تكون قريبة من التشابه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An additional explanation says the trees resemble one another while their fruits differ.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يقول : الأشجار متشابهة والثمار مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's example is one grape cluster: most berries are ripe, sweet and pleasant, while a few remain green, sour and astringent.
rows.anchor: تأخذ العنقود من العنب فترى جميع حباته مدركة نضيجة حلوة طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs for being alike, اشتبه and تشابه, can mean the same as استوى and تساوى; the two verb patterns often overlap.
rows.anchor: يقال : اشتبه الشيآن وتشابها كقولك استويا وتساويا ، والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed reading has متشابها وغير متشابه in place of the verse's wording.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { متشابها وغير متشابه } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular مشتبها instead of a dual can either describe only one of the paired items or elide a repeated description, applying similarity and difference to both olive and pomegranate; a poetic line illustrates the construction.
rows.anchor: إنما قال مشتبها ولم يقل مشتبهين إما اكتفاء بوصف أحدهما

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read ثمره with both ث and م vocalized u; it can be the plural of ثمرة, as خشبة becomes خشب, supported by Quran 63:4 and a line about hills.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي { ثمره } بضم الثاء والميم ،

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: A second analysis of their reading makes ثمر a collective plural formed by first pluralizing ثمرة as ثمار and then pluralizing that collective.
rows.anchor: أن يكون جمع ثمرة على ثمار . ثم جمع ثمارا على ثمر فيكون ثمر جمع الجمع

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads ثمره with ث vocalized u and م unvocalized, explained as a lightened form, like the differing vocalization of رسل.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة أبي عمرو فوجهها أن تخفيف ثمر ثمر كقولهم : رسل ورسل

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers open both consonants; ثمر is then the collective plural of ثمرة, like بقرة/بقر, شجرة/شجر and خرزة/خرز.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة الباقين فوجهها : أن الثمر جمع ثمرة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi glosses yanca as ripeness.
rows.anchor: والبحث الثاني : قال الواحدي : الينع النضج

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والليث
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda gives yaneʿ/yīneʿ with fatḥa in the past and kasra in the present; al-Layth lists yanat, ayneʿat and forms with both ya vowels, plus participles yāniʿ and mūniʿ.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : يقال ينع يينع ، بالفتح في الماضي والكسر في المستقبل . وقال الليث :

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف وابن محيصن
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari notes a reading with yaḍamma in وينعه; Ibn Muhaysin reads ويانعه.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وقرىء { وينعه } بضم الياء ، وقرأ ابن محيصن { * ويانعه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking at the fruit when it first appears examines its beginning; looking at ripeness examines its completion, which is the main proof intended by the verse.
rows.anchor: أمر بالنظر في حال الثمر في أول حدوثها . وقوله : { وينعه } أمر بالنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruits and blossoms change from their initial qualities to opposites as they mature: green turns dark or red, sour turns sweet, and sometimes cold becomes hot.
rows.anchor: لا تبقى على حالاتها الأولى ، بل تنتقل إلى أحوال مضادة للأحوال السابقة ، مثل أنها كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These diverse changes need a cause; because nature, seasons, stars and spheres relate similarly to unlike bodies, they cannot explain different outcomes, which must be attributed to a choosing, wise and merciful governor.
rows.anchor: النسب المتشابهة لا يمكن أن تكون أسبابا لحدوث الحوادث المختلفة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says the signs address those seeking faith in God, since the evidence is available to believer and unbeliever alike.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : المراد لمن يطلب الإيمان بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that believers alone are named because they benefit from the sign, as with the description of guidance for the mindful in 2:2.
rows.anchor: وجه تخصيص المؤمنين بالذكر أنهم الذين انتفعوا به دون غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the sign proves a capable, choosing God clearly, yet benefits only those for whom God decrees faith; those decreed to unbelief gain nothing from it.
rows.anchor: قوة الدليل لا تفيد ولا تنفع إلا إذا قدر الله للعبد حصول الإيمان

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes this as proof that anyone who permits what God forbids, or forbids what God permits, is a polytheist by setting up a ruler besides God.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : وفيه دليل على أن كل من أهل شيئا مما

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbi argues that iman names all obedience, despite its lexical sense of assent, just as shirk can name all opposition to God, since obeying idolaters about carrion is called shirk.
rows.anchor: قال الكعبي : الآية حجة على أن الإيمان اسم لجميع الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says shirk here might mean belief that God has a partner in rule and religious obligation, so this usage would still concern belief alone.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يكون المراد من الشرك ههنا اعتقاد أن الله تعالى شريكا في الحكم والتكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying that idolaters dispute with believers about religion, the passage gives a parable contrasting guided believers with lost unbelievers.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر في الآية الأولى أن المشركين يجادلون المؤمنين في دين الله ذكر مثلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided believer is like someone made alive and given light to find his interests; the unbeliever remains immersed in darkness, endlessly bewildered.
rows.anchor: فبين أن المؤمن المهتدي بمنزلة من كان ميتا ، فجعل حيا بعد ذلك وأعطى نورا يهتدى به في مصالحه

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's school says God is the one who adorns unbelievers' deeds: action depends on a motivating judgment of greater benefit, and God creates that motive.
rows.anchor: فقال أصحابنا : ذلك المزين هو الله تعالى ، ودليله ما سبق ذكره من أن الفعل يتوقف على حصول الداعي

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والحسن
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila say Satan adorns the deeds; they quote al-Hasan as saying that the one who adorned them was Satan.
rows.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : ذلك المزين هو الشيطان ، وحكوا عن الحسن أنه قال : زينه لهم والله الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects Satan as the sole adornment: his prior proof points to God; assigning Satan's unbelief to another satan causes an infinite regress; and 6:108 and 6:123 explicitly attribute adornment or placement of criminals to God.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا في غاية الضعف لوجوه : الأول : الدليل القاطع

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ reads ميتا with a doubled ya; the other readers lighten it, and language scholars say both forms have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع { ميتا } مشددا ، والباقون مخففا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses call unbelievers dead and contrast life with death (16:21, 36:70, 27:80, 35:19, 35:22); Razi says disbelief is death because ignorance causes perplexity and stillness, while guidance is knowledge and insight leading to salvation.
rows.anchor: فلما جعل الكفر موتا والكافر ميتا ، جعل الهدى حياة والمهتدي حيا ، وإنما جعل الكفر موتا لأنه جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because جعلنا له نورا is coordinated with فأحييناه, the light must signify something distinct from the life.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله { فأحييناه } فوجب أن يكون هذا النور مغايرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi models knowledge in four soul-stages: initial capacity to receive knowledge, primary universal axioms, acquired theoretical knowledge available for recall, and sacred insights present and illuminating the spirit; the first stage is called death.
rows.anchor: الأرواح البشرية لها أربع مراتب في المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Razi's four-stage model, primary universal knowledge is life, reasoning from axioms to theory is the light, and actively present sacred insights are walking by it; this completes the soul's happiness.
rows.anchor: المرتبة الثانية : وهي أن تحصل العلوم البديهية الكلية فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading calls life the soul's readiness and light the arrival of revelation: as sight needs a sound sense and sunlight, spiritual vision needs sound reason and revelation.
rows.anchor: الحياة عبارة عن الاستعداد القائم بجوهر الروح ، والنور عبارة عن إيصال نور الوحي

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Other commentators identify the light as the Quran, the light of religion, or the light of wisdom; Razi says these are close but prefers his earlier account.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : المراد بهذا النور ، القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person continually immersed in ignorance and blameworthy traits makes those darknesses seem innate and hard to remove; darkness also leaves him confused, afraid and helpless.
rows.anchor: إذا دام كون الكافر في ظلمات الجهل والأخلاق الذميمة صارت تلك الظلمات كالصفة الذاتية اللازمة له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns Hamza and Abu Jahl: after Abu Jahl threw dung at Muhammad, Hamza returned from hunting, struck Abu Jahl with his bow, condemned idol worship and declared faith; Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : إن أبا جهل رمى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بفرث

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the verse concerns Muhammad and Abu Jahl, who said he would not believe unless revelation came to him as it came to the Prophet; Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : نزلت هذه الآية في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي جهل

rows.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي
rows.claim: Ikrima and al-Kalbi say the verse was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir and Abu Jahl; Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة والكلبي : نزلت في عمار بن ياسر وأبي جهل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl; Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب وأبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers a general application to every believer and unbeliever because the meaning fits everyone; since the sura descended all at once, particular occasions are difficult to assert without a prophetic statement specifying an individual.
rows.anchor: إن هذه الآية عامة في حق جميع المؤمنين والكافرين ، وهذا هو الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that faith and disbelief come from God: life and light mean knowledge and guidance, motives are divinely created, and a person seeking knowledge but getting ignorance must have had the opposite produced in him; blaming error on mistaking it for knowledge regresses to prior ignorance unless some is created externally.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية من أقوى الدلائل أيضا على أن الكفر والإيمان من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of deeds keeps a person from abandoning action: soul and body affect one another, so sustained good works imprint fitting qualities on the soul, and the spiritual wayfarer cannot dispense with action.
rows.anchor: فإذا واظب الإنسان على أعمال البر والخير ظهرت الآثار المناسبة لها في جوهر النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing those who follow the straight path, God sets the people of the Garden against the people of the Fire, placing warning after promise.
rows.anchor: حال من يتمسك بالصراط المستقيم ، بين بعده حال من يكون بالضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative يوم depends on an omitted verb: remember the day; or it belongs with We gather and say; or We gather and say are coordinated; the event is too terrible to describe.
rows.anchor: { ويوم يحشرهم } منصوب بمحذوف ، أي واذكر يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the pronoun as all morally responsible beings whom God will resurrect, though they were not mentioned immediately before.
rows.anchor: يعودإلى المعلوم ، لا إلى المذكور ، وهو الثقلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the pronoun as the devils mentioned at 6:112.
rows.anchor: في قوله : { وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبى عدوا شياطين الإنس والجن يوحى بعضهم إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted phrase means We gather them, then God says O company of jinn; His speech after the gathering rebukes them and makes them admit guilt after worldly defiance.
rows.anchor: في الآية محذوف والتقدير : يوم نحشرهم جميعا فنقول : يا معشر الجن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead supplies a passive it is said to them, since he considers direct divine speech to unbelievers unlikely in light of 2:174.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : التقدير فيقال لهم يا معشر الجن ، لأنه يبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn cannot literally multiply human beings, since only God creates bodies and life; the phrase means they called many humans toward misguidance and found them receptive.
rows.anchor: هذا لا بد فيه من التأويل . لأن الجن لا يقدرون على الاستكثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text also implicitly rebukes the human allies: jinn invited them, humans accepted, and both shared in the wrongdoing; the verse then reports the humans' answer.
rows.anchor: فكما قال للجن تبكيتا ، فكذلك قال للإنس توبيخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human allies describe themselves as absorbed in worldly benefits and pleasures until they reached this point and became certain of their bad end.
rows.anchor: فوصفوا أنفسهم بالتوفر على منافع الدنيا ، والاستمتاع بلذاتها

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة والكلبي وابن جريج
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Ikrima, al-Kalbi and Ibn Jurayj say humans sought a jinn valley-master's protection while traveling, and jinn enjoyed being revered and boasting of their mastery; this is linked to 72:6.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن وعكرمة والكلبي وابن جريج واحتجوا على صحته بقوله تعالى : { وأنه كان رجال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers that humans obeyed jinn as leaders, benefiting them through service, while jinn drew humans toward desires and pleasures; this better explains jinn's many human followers than the rare valley-protection custom.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول اختيار الزجاج . قال : وهذا أولى من الوجه المتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second overall interpretation takes the statement as humans enjoying one another, since mutual enjoyment between humans is common and the speakers are human allies of jinn.
rows.anchor: هو كلام الإنس خاصة ، لأن استمتاع الجن بالإنس وبالعكس أمر قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say their mutual enjoyment lasted until its fixed endpoint, after which failure, regret and remorse arrived too late.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : أن ذلك الاستمتاع كان حاصلا إلى أجل معين ووقت محدود ،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view identifies the appointed term as death; its proponents say the verse shows that every person, murdered or not, dies at an appointed time.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : هو وقت الموت .

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view identifies the appointed term as the time of release and empowerment.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : هو وقت التخلية والتمكين

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A third view identifies the appointed term as the time of reckoning on the Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم : المراد وقت المحاسبة في القيامة
